scores.reason: Measure type: unspecified total insulin plus C-peptide, with PEG precipitation and insulin autoantibodies. Insulin and C-peptide immunoassays are widely available, but the ADA workgroup found among-assay CV of 12% to 66% (median 24%) on 2007-era platforms, and antibody-complex interference differs by assay (one assay did not show recovery loss after PEG). PEG precipitation is a lab-developed step with no standard protocol and insulin autoantibody testing is often send-out. Alternative bin 1 if PEG and IAA are counted as the core test. Older-generation and non-US assay data, so confidence capped at medium (clarification 20).
sources: PMID 42662728 DOI 10.1016/j.metop.2026.100491 abstract (listed in project files)

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting-based (fasting insulin or HOMA-IR) after gestational diabetes; the project found no insulin test in the pathway, so this scores the assay a research use would need. Fasting insulin immunoassays are widely available but unstandardized (ADA workgroup among-assay CV median 24%, 2007 platforms; bias over 15.5% vs IDMS for 7 of 10 methods in 2009). The comparator glucose and A1C tests would score 3 or 4. Not determinable from files whether post-load measures were used. Older-generation data, confidence low.

Measure type: C-peptide (fasting) as a remission-score input. C-peptide is a widely available immunoassay, but results differ between methods and laboratories, especially at higher concentrations, and a 2025 review still calls for standardization; the score cutoff is study-specific. Not a standard test with common cutoffs, so 2 not 3. Unreliable with insulin therapy or CKD (project files). Interlaboratory evidence is from 2007 assays plus a 2025 review (abstract only).
sources: PMID 22963817 (project files, abstract; DOI not re-checked here)

scores.reason: Measure type: C-peptide, stimulated (MMTT 2-h or 4-h AUC). Assay is widely available but unstandardized between methods (PMID 17332147); the test needs a timed multi-sample protocol, which fits anchor 2. Trials run it in central or protocolised settings. MMTT is described in current trial protocols as the primary endpoint, so the protocol is established for research, not a routine laboratory order. Confidence medium because the 2004/2008 MMTT consensus papers in the project files were not re-read here.
sources: PMID 38950997 DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-084808 abstract (2-h MMTT primary outcome)
PMID 14693724 and PMID 18628574 (project files, abstract; DOIs not re-checked here)

scores.reason: Measure type: unspecified insulin and C-peptide in an infant, with PEG precipitation of maternal and infant samples. Needs a critical-sample draw in a small infant, paired maternal sample, a lab-developed PEG step and often send-out antibody testing; assay-specific interference (IgM, non-IAA antibodies) is documented only in a 2026 review and case reports. No validated protocol or recovery cutoff found in the screened records. Alternative bin 2 if the lab offers PEG routinely.

Measure type: C-peptide, stimulated (MMTT) around total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplant. Assay widely available but unstandardized; a timed protocol is needed and it is run at a few high-volume centres. A 2022 survey of transplant programs reports that monitoring practices are not standardized. No preoperative threshold found in the project files (row 27 notes). Alternative bin 1 if only specialised centres are counted.
sources: PMID 23890130 and PMID 38895780 (project files, abstract; DOIs not re-checked here)

scores.reason: Measure type: post-load (5-h 75 g OGTT) and mixed-meal glucose with insulin. Glucose is a standard test, but the 5-h OGTT and MMTT need a long timed protocol with no standardized glucose cutoff (authors set 55 mg/dL themselves, per project files), and the added insulin measurement is an unstandardized immunoassay (PMID 17272483). Fits anchor 2.
sources: PMID 33916952 DOI 10.3390/jpm11040276 (project files, abstract and full-text windows)

anchor_issues: D4 rows 20 and 25: the anchors do not say whether to score the core assay (insulin, C-peptide) or the add-on step (PEG precipitation, IAA). I scored the whole test needed for the use; the core assay alone would be 2.
D4 rows 8 and 27: anchor 2 combines 'unstandardized' and 'needs a timed protocol'; MMTT C-peptide has both. Anchor 1 (specialised) could also apply to transplant centres; I chose 2.

D4 row 45: the use case records no insulin test, so I scored the assay a research use would need (fasting insulin or HOMA-IR); the case could also be read as not determinable or as the OGTT/A1C pathway (3 to 4).
assumptions: Fasting insulin or HOMA-IR is the measure for row 45; post-load measures were not assumed.
US-marketed assay performance is inferred from the 2007 and 2009 ADA workgroup data, 2024 and 2025 papers, which include non-US and older platforms; confidence capped at medium (clarification 20).
